To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rat produces enhanced amounts of prostacyclin (PGI2), a potent hypotension substance, by its aorta.
aortic rings and aortic homogenate from spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR) have a higher capacity to convert arachidonate into prostacyclin (PGI2) than aortae of normal rats (NR).
PGI2 is synthesized in aortic tissue and its formation is enhanced in the spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formation of PGI 2, a potent vasodepressor substance, by the aorta of the spontaneously hypertenisve rat.
the identification of PGI2 as a potent vasodepressor substance formed from arachidonic acids in aortic tissue of the SHR.
the identification of a possible mechanism of action of norepinephrines and other catecholamines, and with the possible involvement of PGI2 as a mediator of this action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PGI2 synthetic capacity is enhanced in the SHR.

the enhanced formation of PGI in SHR reflects the presence of a greater number of enzyme molecules available to the substrate and that this is a compensatory response to the high levels of circulating catecholamines.
the enhanced PGI2 formation by the hypertensive vascular tissue represents an adaptive response to an elevated circulating catecholamine level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SHR has an increased number of PGI2 synthase molecules in its aortic tissue.
the SHR has a PGI2 synthetic pathway which is more responsive to the stimulation by norepinepherine.
the SHR is a model of enhanced PGI2 production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of PGI 2, a potent vasodilatory prostaglandin, is enhanced in the spontaneously hypertensive rats.
aortic PGI2 is increased in SHR and that this increase is related to increased levels of catecholinamines in these animals.

the formation of PGI 2 by aortic rings of spontaneously hypertensive rats is enhanced and that this enhanced PGI 2 formation may be due to an increased sensitivity of the vascular PGI 2 system to norepinephrime.
